title: Prakrama 2, Sarga 6. [The Greatness of Advaita]
html:
The Lord with His club threatens the haters of devotees; the world as a great forest; Advaita's arrival and dance; the Lord promises love to His children; the greatness of Advaita-Kamalaksha; the doctrine of the Self forbidden

Verse 1

अथापरदिने तत्राद्वैताचार्यो महायशाः।
नवद्वीपे समायातो द्रष्टुं विश्वम्भरेश्वरम्॥१॥

athāparadine tatrādvaitācāryo mahāyaśāḥ|
navadvīpe samāyāto draṣṭuṁ viśvambhareśvaram||1||

atha — then; apara-dine — on another day; tatra — there; advaita-acharyah — Advaita Acharya; maha-yashah — the greatly renowned; navadvipe — to Navadvipa; samayatah — came; drashtum — to see; vishvambhara-ishvaram — the Lord Vishvambhara.

1On another day the greatly renowned Advaita Acharya came to Navadvipa to see the Lord Vishvambhara.

Verse 2

स्नानं कृत्वार्चयित्वेशं स यावद्गच्छतीश्वरः।
द्रष्टुं तावत्स भगवाञ्छ्रीवासस्याश्रमे वसन्॥२॥

snānaṁ kṛtvārcayitveśaṁ sa yāvadgacchatīśvaraḥ|
draṣṭuṁ tāvatsa bhagavāñchrīvāsasyāśrame vasan||2||

snanam — bath; kritva — having taken; archayitva — having worshipped; isham — the Lord; sah — he; yavat — while; gachchhati — goes; ishvarah — the lord; drashtum — to see; tavat — meanwhile; sah — He; bhagavan — Bhagavan; shrivasasya — of Srivasa; ashrame — in the abode; vasan — staying.

2While He, having bathed and worshipped the Lord, was on His way to see Him, Bhagavan, who was staying in Srivasa's abode,

Verse 3

पुष्पकं न्यस्य दण्डाग्रे प्रोवाच सस्मिताननः।
गदापूजा कृता ह्येषा मया दुष्टस्य शासनम्॥३॥

puṣpakaṁ nyasya daṇḍāgre provāca sasmitānanaḥ|
gadāpūjā kṛtā hyeṣā mayā duṣṭasya śāsanam||3||

pushpakam — a little flower; nyasya — placing; danda-agre — on the tip of a staff; provacha — said; sa-smita-ananah — with a smiling face; gada-puja — worship of the club; krita — has been done; hi — indeed; esha — this; maya — by Me; dushtasya — of the wicked; shasanam — the chastisement.

3placed a flower on the tip of a staff and said with a smile: "So I have worshipped My club. It is the chastisement of the wicked:

Verse 4

करिष्याम्यनया नित्यं मद्भक्तद्वेषिणः सदा।
भक्त एव सदा मह्यं प्राणाधिको न संशयः॥४॥

kariṣyāmyanayā nityaṁ madbhaktadveṣiṇaḥ sadā|
bhakta eva sadā mahyaṁ prāṇādhiko na saṁśayaḥ||4||

karishyami — I shall carry out (the chastisement); anaya — with it; nityam — ever; mat-bhakta-dveshinah — of the haters of My devotees; sada — constantly; bhaktah — the devotee; eva — indeed; sada — always; mahyam — to Me; prana-adhikah — dearer than life; na samshayah — there is no doubt.

4with it I shall always chastise those who hate My devotees. For a devotee is ever dearer to Me than life — of this there is no doubt.

Verse 5

एकोऽस्ति दुष्टो मद्भक्तद्वेषिणं कुष्ठरोगिणम्।
कृत्वा तं पुनरेवाहं पैशाचनरकाश्रयम्॥५॥

eko'sti duṣṭo madbhaktadveṣiṇaṁ kuṣṭharogiṇam|
kṛtvā taṁ punarevāhaṁ paiśācanarakāśrayam||5||

ekah — one; asti — there is; dushtah — wicked man; mat-bhakta-dveshinam — the hater of My devotees; kushtha-roginam — a leper; kritva — having made; tam — him; punah eva — then; aham — I; paishacha-naraka-ashrayam — a dweller in the hell of the pishachas.

5There is a certain wicked man1 here, a hater of My devotees. I shall make him a leper, and then —

Verse 6

करिष्याम्यचिरं कालं सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम्।
नाशयिष्यामि तच्छिष्यान्विधास्ये विड्भुजानहम्॥६॥

kariṣyāmyaciraṁ kālaṁ satyametanmayoditam|
nāśayiṣyāmi tacchiṣyānvidhāsye viḍbhujānaham||6||

karishyami — I shall make; achiram kalam — before long; satyam — the truth; etat — this; maya — by Me; uditam — spoken; nashayishyami — I shall destroy; tat-shishyan — his disciples; vidhasye — I shall make; vid-bhujan — eaters of filth; aham — I.

6before long — a dweller in the hell of the pishachas: this I say in truth. And his disciples too I shall destroy, turning them into eaters of filth.

Verse 7

वनं प्रयातुमिच्छामि तदत्रैव महद्वनम्।
व्याघ्रस्य सदृशाः केचित्केचित्पाषाणसन्निभाः॥७॥

vanaṁ prayātumicchāmi tadatraiva mahadvanam|
vyāghrasya sadṛśāḥ kecitkecitpāṣāṇasannibhāḥ||7||

vanam — to the forest; prayatum — to go; ichchhami — I wish; tat — but; atra eva — right here; mahat — a great; vanam — forest; vyaghrasya — to a tiger; sadrishah — alike; kechit — some; kechit — others; pashana-sannibhah — like stones.

7I wish to go away to the forest — yet here too is a great forest: some are like tigers, others like stones,

Verse 8

वृक्षाणां सन्निभाः केचित्केचित्तृणनिभा नराः।
पशूनां सन्निभाः केचित्तेनेदं सुमहद्वनम्॥८॥

vṛkṣāṇāṁ sannibhāḥ kecitkecittṛṇanibhā narāḥ|
paśūnāṁ sannibhāḥ kecittenedaṁ sumahadvanam||8||

vrikshanam — to trees; sannibhah — alike; kechit — some; kechit — others; trina-nibhah — like grass; narah — men; pashunam — to beasts; sannibhah — alike; kechit — some; tena — therefore; idam — this; su-mahat — very great; vanam — forest.

8some like trees, some men like grass, and some like beasts. And so this world is a vast forest.

Verse 9

श्रीकृष्णचरणाम्भोजमधुपानरता हि ये।
ते मनुजाः समाख्याताः सर्वजीवोपकारिणः॥९॥

śrīkṛṣṇacaraṇāmbhojamadhupānaratā hi ye|
te manujāḥ samākhyātāḥ sarvajīvopakāriṇaḥ||9||

shri-krishna-charana-ambhoja-madhu-pana-ratah — delighting in drinking the honey of Sri Krishna's lotus feet; hi — but; ye — who; te — they; manujah — human beings; samakhyatah — are called; sarva-jiva-upakarinah — benefactors of all beings.

9But those who delight in drinking the honey of Sri Krishna's lotus feet — they alone are called human beings, the benefactors of all creatures.

Verse 10

अद्वैताचार्यवर्योऽत्र समायात इति श्रुतम्।
कथं नायाति यत्रास्ते तत्र गच्छामहे वयम्॥१०॥

advaitācāryavaryo'tra samāyāta iti śrutam|
kathaṁ nāyāti yatrāste tatra gacchāmahe vayam||10||

advaita-acharya-varyah — Advaita, the best of acharyas; atra — here; samayatah — has arrived; iti — thus; shrutam — it is heard; katham — why; na ayati — does he not come; yatra — where; aste — he stays; tatra — there; gachchhamahe — let us go; vayam — we.

10I have heard that Advaita, the best of acharyas, has arrived here. Why then does He not come? Let us go to Him, to where He is staying."

Verse 11

एतस्मिन्समये तत्राचार्यः स्वयमुपागतः।
उपायनं समादाय तत्पादपद्मसन्निधौ॥११॥

etasminsamaye tatrācāryaḥ svayamupāgataḥ|
upāyanaṁ samādāya tatpādapadmasannidhau||11||

etasmin samaye — at that time; tatra — there; acharyah — the Acharya; svayam — himself; upagatah — arrived; upayanam — a gift; samadaya — taking; tat-pada-padma-sannidhau — before His lotus feet.

11At that very moment the Acharya Himself arrived there, bearing a gift; He offered it at the Lord's lotus feet

Verse 12

तद्दत्त्वा दण्डवद्भूमौ निपपात तदा प्रभुः।
करे गृहीत्वा तं प्राह त्वदर्थोऽहमिहागतः॥१२॥

taddattvā daṇḍavadbhūmau nipapāta tadā prabhuḥ|
kare gṛhītvā taṁ prāha tvadartho'hamihāgataḥ||12||

tat — it; dattva — having offered; dandavat — like a stick; bhumau — to the ground; nipapata — he fell; tada — then; prabhuh — the Lord; kare — by the hand; grihitva — taking; tam — him; praha — said; tvat-arthah — for your sake; aham — I; iha — here; agatah — have come.

12and fell to the ground like a stick. Then the Lord took Him by the hand and said: "It is for Your sake that I have come here."2

Verse 13

इत्युक्त्वा हर्षयित्वा तत्खट्वायां समुपाविशत्।
आज्ञया तस्य देवस्याद्वैताचार्यो ननर्त ह॥१३॥

ityuktvā harṣayitvā tatkhaṭvāyāṁ samupāviśat|
ājñayā tasya devasyādvaitācāryo nanarta ha||13||

iti — thus; uktva — having said; harshayitva — having gladdened (him); tat — then; khatvayam — on a cot; samupavishat — sat down; ajnaya — by the command; tasya — of that; devasya — Lord; advaita-acharyah — Advaita Acharya; nanarta — danced; ha — indeed.

13Having said this and gladdened Him, the Lord sat down on a cot, and at His command Advaita Acharya began to dance.

Verse 14

तद्दृष्ट्वा भगवान्प्रीतस्तं प्राह तव बालकाः।
एते मां प्रार्थयन्त्येव प्रेमभक्तिं सुदुर्लभाम्॥१४॥

taddṛṣṭvā bhagavānprītastaṁ prāha tava bālakāḥ|
ete māṁ prārthayantyeva premabhaktiṁ sudurlabhām||14||

tat — that; drishtva — seeing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; pritah — pleased; tam — to him; praha — said; tava — your; balakah — children; ete — these; mam — Me; prarthayanti eva — are begging for; prema-bhaktim — loving devotion; su-durlabham — so hard to attain.

14Seeing this, Bhagavan was pleased and said to Him: "These children of Yours are begging Me for loving devotion, so hard to attain.

Verse 15

दास्यामि त्वत्कृते वत्स तच्छ्रुत्वा हर्षसंप्लुतः।
आचार्यः प्राह भगवन्नेते ते चरणानुगाः।
कारुण्यालय वात्सल्यात्तव किं स्यात्सुदुर्लभम्॥१५॥

dāsyāmi tvatkṛte vatsa tacchrutvā harṣasaṁplutaḥ|
ācāryaḥ prāha bhagavannete te caraṇānugāḥ|
kāruṇyālaya vātsalyāttava kiṁ syātsudurlabham||15||

dasyami — I shall give; tvat-krite — for your sake; vatsa — child; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; harsha-samplutah — flooded with joy; acharyah — the Acharya; praha — said; bhagavan — O Bhagavan; ete — these; te — Your; charana-anugah — followers of Your feet; karunya-alaya — O abode of compassion; vatsalyat — by the affection; tava — Your; kim — what; syat — could be; su-durlabham — hard to attain.

15For Your sake, child, I shall give it." Hearing this, the Acharya, flooded with joy, replied: "O Bhagavan, they are followers of Your feet. O abode of compassion, what could be beyond their reach when You love them?"

Verse 16

अथोपविष्टास्ते सर्वे पार्श्वतस्तस्य चक्रिणः।
ज्योत्स्नावत्यां रजन्यां च पुनराह महाभुजः॥१६॥

athopaviṣṭāste sarve pārśvatastasya cakriṇaḥ|
jyotsnāvatyāṁ rajanyāṁ ca punarāha mahābhujaḥ||16||

atha — then; upavishtah — sat down; te — they; sarve — all; parshvatah — beside; tasya — that; chakrinah — Holder of the discus; jyotsna-vatyam — moonlit; rajanyam — in the night; cha — and; punah — again; aha — spoke; maha-bhujah — the Mighty-armed.

16Then all sat down beside the Holder of the discus; and in that moonlit night the Mighty-armed spoke again:

Verse 17

कमलाक्षोऽसि मेऽतीव भक्तस्त्वत्कृत एव हि।
समागतोऽहं त्वं नृत्यगीतेन सुसुखी भव॥१७॥

kamalākṣo'si me'tīva bhaktastvatkṛta eva hi|
samāgato'haṁ tvaṁ nṛtyagītena susukhī bhava||17||

kamalakshah — Kamalaksha; asi — you are; me — My; ativa — utmost; bhaktah — devotee; tvat-krite — for your sake; eva hi — indeed; samagatah — have come; aham — I; tvam — you; nritya-gitena — with dance and song; su-sukhi — happy; bhava — be.

17"Kamalaksha3, You are My foremost devotee: it is for Your sake that I have come. So be happy, dancing and singing."

Verse 18

तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवद्वाक्यं श्रीमच्छ्रीवासपण्डितः।
उवाच मधुरैर्वाक्यैर्विनीतस्तत्पदाम्बुजे॥१८॥

tacchrutvā bhagavadvākyaṁ śrīmacchrīvāsapaṇḍitaḥ|
uvāca madhurairvākyairvinītastatpadāmbuje||18||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; bhagavat-vakyam — the word of Bhagavan; shrimat-shrivasa-panditah — Sriman Srivasa Pandita; uvacha — spoke; madhuraih vakyaih — with sweet words; vinitah — humbly bowing; tat-pada-ambuje — at His lotus feet.

18Hearing these words of Bhagavan, Sriman Srivasa Pandita, humbly bowing at His lotus feet, spoke in sweet words:

Verse 19

किं तेऽसौ भगवन्भक्तः करुणेयं तव प्रभो।
तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान्क्रुद्धस्तं निर्भर्त्स्याभ्यभाषत॥१९॥

kiṁ te'sau bhagavanbhaktaḥ karuṇeyaṁ tava prabho|
tacchrutvā bhagavānkruddhastaṁ nirbhartsyābhyabhāṣata||19||

kim — is it that; te — Your; asau — he; bhagavan — O Bhagavan; bhaktah — devotee; karuna — mercy; iyam — this; tava — Your; prabho — O Lord; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; kruddhah — angry; tam — him; nirbhartsya — rebuking; abhyabhashata — said.

19"Is He really Your devotee, O Bhagavan? It is only Your mercy, O Lord!" Hearing this, Bhagavan grew angry, rebuked him, and said:

Verse 20

किमुद्धवस्तथाक्रूरो भक्तो मेऽतीववत्सलः।
आचार्योऽयं ततो न्यूनः किमेवं त्वं प्रभाषसे॥२०॥

kimuddhavastathākrūro bhakto me'tīvavatsalaḥ|
ācāryo'yaṁ tato nyūnaḥ kimevaṁ tvaṁ prabhāṣase||20||

kim — is it that; uddhavah — Uddhava; tatha — and; akrurah — Akrura; bhaktah — a devotee; me — to Me; ativa-vatsalah — exceedingly loving; acharyah — Acharya; ayam — this; tatah — than they; nyunah — lower; kim — why; evam — thus; tvam — you; prabhashase — speak.

20"Are Uddhava and Akrura4 My devotees of boundless love, and is this Acharya beneath them? Why do you speak so?

Verse 21

किं वा भारतवर्षेऽस्मिन्नाचार्यस्य समोऽपरः।
वर्तते कोऽपि मद्भक्तो यस्मादज्ञो द्विजो भवान्॥२१॥

kiṁ vā bhāratavarṣe'sminnācāryasya samo'paraḥ|
vartate ko'pi madbhakto yasmādajño dvijo bhavān||21||

kim va — or else; bharata-varshe — in Bharata-varsha; asmin — this; acharyasya — to the Acharya; samah — equal; aparah — another; vartate — is there; kah api — anyone; mat-bhaktah — devotee of Mine; yasmat — since (you say so); ajnah — ignorant; dvijah — brahmana; bhavan — you are.

21Or is there some other devotee of Mine in this Bharata-varsha equal to the Acharya? Since you speak so, you are an ignorant brahmana!"

Verse 22

तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवद्वाक्यं भीत्या तूष्णीं बभूव ह॥२२॥

tacchrutvā bhagavadvākyaṁ bhītyā tūṣṇīṁ babhūva ha||22||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; bhagavat-vakyam — the word of Bhagavan; bhitya — out of fear; tushnim — silent; babhuva — became; ha — indeed.

22Hearing these words of Bhagavan, he fell silent out of fear.

Verse 23

ततः प्रोवाच भगवानध्यात्मं न कदाचन।
भवद्भिः कुत्रचिद्वापि वक्तव्यं यदि रोच्यते॥२३॥

tataḥ provāca bhagavānadhyātmaṁ na kadācana|
bhavadbhiḥ kutracidvāpi vaktavyaṁ yadi rocyate||23||

tatah — then; provacha — said; bhagavan — Bhagavan; adhyatmam — adhyatma (the doctrine of the Self); na kadachana — never; bhavadbhih — by you; kutrachit va api — anywhere; vaktavyam — is to be spoken; yadi — if; rochyate — it pleases.

23Then Bhagavan said: "Never, anywhere, are you to speak of the doctrine of the Self5. And if it is to your taste,

Verse 24

तदा प्रेमा न दातव्यो भवद्भ्यः सत्यमेव हि॥२४॥

tadā premā na dātavyo bhavadbhyaḥ satyameva hi||24||

tada — then; prema — love; na datavyah — is not to be given; bhavadbhyah — to you; satyam eva hi — this is the very truth.

24then love will not be given to you — this is the very truth."

Verse 25

तच्छ्रुत्वा पण्डितः प्राह श्रीवासो जगदीश्वरम्।
तत्र मे विस्मृतिर्भूयाद्यथाहं न वदामि तत्॥२५॥

tacchrutvā paṇḍitaḥ prāha śrīvāso jagadīśvaram|
tatra me vismṛtirbhūyādyathāhaṁ na vadāmi tat||25||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; panditah — the Pandita; praha — said; shrivasah — Srivasa; jagat-ishvaram — to the Lord of the world; tatra — of that; me — in me; vismritih — forgetfulness; bhuyat — may there be; yatha — so that; aham — I; na vadami — do not speak; tat — of it.

25Hearing this, Srivasa Pandita said to the Lord of the world: "May I forget it, so that I never speak of it."

Verse 26

मुरारिः प्राह भगवन्नध्यात्मं न विदाम्यहम्।
तं प्राह देवो जानासि कमलाक्षाच्छ्रुतं हि तत्॥२६॥

murāriḥ prāha bhagavannadhyātmaṁ na vidāmyaham|
taṁ prāha devo jānāsi kamalākṣācchrutaṁ hi tat||26||

murarih — Murari; praha — said; bhagavan — O Bhagavan; adhyatmam — adhyatma; na vidami — do not know; aham — I; tam — to him; praha — said; devah — the Lord; janasi — you know it; kamalakshat — from Kamalaksha; shrutam — heard; hi — for; tat — that.

26Murari said: "O Bhagavan, I do not know the doctrine of the Self." The Lord replied to him: "You do — for you have heard it from Kamalaksha."6

Verse 27

इति सपदि निशम्य देववाक्यं प्रमुदितमनसो बभूवुरार्याः।
हरिहरपदपद्मसीधुमत्ता ननृतुरनिमिषा इवोत्सवाढ्याः॥२७॥

iti sapadi niśamya devavākyaṁ pramuditamanaso babhūvurāryāḥ|
hariharapadapadmasīdhumattā nanṛturanimiṣā ivotsavāḍhyāḥ||27||

iti — thus; sapadi — at once; nishamya — hearing; deva-vakyam — the word of the Lord; pramudita-manasah — glad at heart; babhuvuh — became; aryah — the noble; hari-hara-pada-padma-sidhu-mattah — intoxicated with the wine of the lotus feet of Harihara; nanrituh — danced; animishah — the unblinking ones (gods); iva — like; utsava-adhyah — rich in festivity.

27Hearing at once these words of the Lord, the noble ones rejoiced at heart and, intoxicated with the wine of the lotus feet of Harihara7, danced like the gods at a splendid festival.

Thus ends the sixth sarga of the second prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Possibly the brahmana Gopala Chapala, struck with leprosy for offending Srivasa (his story is told in the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 17).
  2. According to tradition, the Lord descended in answer to the prayers of Advaita Acharya.
  3. Kamalaksha is the worldly name of Advaita Acharya.
  4. Uddhava and Akrura are intimate devotees of Krishna.
  5. Sanskrit adhyatma: the doctrine of the Self and its identity with Brahman, as the Lord Himself had expounded it in 2.5.20–28, only to set devotion above it at once (2.5.30).
  6. Cf. 2.4.22, where the Lord rebukes Murari for his song on the doctrine of the Self.
  7. Harihara: literally "Hari and Hara." Here, in a canto on Advaita's greatness, probably Hari (Gaura) and Hara (Advaita, revered as one with Sadashiva); it may also be understood as an epithet of Gaura (cf. 2.7.6). Neither reading makes Shiva equal to Vishnu.
